evidence_quote: This paper investigates the main barriers to energy efficiency in Singapore-based industries.
we explicitly considered the effects of energy performance measurement on energy efficiency outcomes and their determinants in the MOA framework

stage1.ineligibility_reason: The paper proposes and empirically tests a behavioural/organisational framework (Motivation, Opportunity, and Ability) explaining the determinants of firms' energy-efficiency adoption outcomes, using a 143-firm industry survey and PLS structural equation modelling. It does not present, propose, evaluate, or characterise an EnPI or EnB measurement model: no energy performance indicator, energy baseline, normalisation variables, functional form, or baseline-construction/estimation approach for energy consumption is defined. Energy performance measurement enters only as an incidental behavioural construct ('monitoring ability') moderating adoption, not as a characterised measurement model. Ineligible under the v2.3 threshold (incidental EnPI/EnB mention; behavioural/decision framework).

paper_type.evidence_quote: We tested this novel framework using data from an industry survey conducted by the Energy Studies Institute, National University of Singapore.

stage1.notes: Behavioural MOA survey/PLS-SEM study of energy-efficiency barriers; no EnPI/EnB model characterised. paper_type='other' (survey framework-test fits no model enum).
